findings.title: Router default conflicts with stated scope
findings.problem: Scope says anything outside the listed in-scope items is out of scope, but the Router defaults ambiguous messages to a product search, so the boundary is unclear for borderline messages.
findings.proof: intent (a product search when in doubt)
findings.fix: State the tie-break explicitly: when in doubt, search only if the message names a kind of product or a product, otherwise ask one clarifying question.

findings.title: Budget loosening can exceed the shopper's hard limit
findings.problem: The system prompt treats a budget as a limit the shopper sets, but the catalog tool silently raises it by 25% or removes it when results are thin, which conflicts with that rule and with precedence level 3.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: Disable budget loosening in the tool (or pass a flag) so the budget is kept as a hard filter, and let the Answerer report the miss and offer a raised budget instead.

findings.title: Human oversight before speech is absent as a control
findings.problem: The context states that no human approves replies and offers only after-the-fact reporting, with no human escalation or stop mechanism for a live voice session, which the governance tier and frameworks call for.
findings.fix: Add an operator-facing kill switch and a rule that the assistant hands over to a human store contact or stops answering when repeated reports or safety flags occur in a session.

findings.title: No rule for a shopper who is a minor
findings.problem: The child rules apply only when the shopper states a child's age, and nothing says how the assistant treats a shopper who says they are a minor or who speaks as one.
findings.fix: Add a rule that a self-declared minor gets age-appropriate product results only and that restricted categories (alcohol, tobacco, adult content) stay declined regardless of who asks.

findings.title: Shopper message is not declared as data in any fence
findings.problem: Tool results and notes are fenced and declared data, but the shopper's transcript reaching the Router and Planner is not placed in a declared fence, leaving that channel's data status implicit.
findings.proof: Tool results and their notes reach a model only inside a fence that its prompt declares data, never instructions
findings.fix: Add a <shopper_message> fence to the Router and Planner prompts and declare it data, and list it alongside the other fences in the Untrusted content section.

findings.title: Tool loosening text duplicated in the system prompt
findings.problem: The rag.search description restates the full loosening order and never-loosened rules, which the system prompt's Search section repeats, so the same rule is paid for twice in every call.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found:
findings.fix: Keep the loosening order in one place (the tool description) and reduce the system prompt to a single reference to it.

findings.title: No worked example of a compliant table row or abstention
findings.problem: The context specifies citation and cell rules in prose but gives no concrete example row, so the Answerer must infer the exact citation format from description alone.
findings.fix: Add one short example table row and one abstention reply with their citation format, kept under 80 tokens.

findings.title: Router paragraph is long and recursive
findings.problem: The Router stage describes a second model pass for buried product requests in one long run-on sentence, a passage that repeats the Retriever and Critic rules and costs tokens on every turn.
findings.proof: A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model for a buried product request
findings.fix: Compress the Router stage to one sentence stating the second-pass rule and drop restatements of the Answerer's behaviour.

findings.title: Spoken short-form sentences duplicated in fixed replies
findings.problem: The shortened spoken variants repeat most of the full fixed replies in the same file, and the system prompt also restates which ids are shortened, so the same wording appears in two places.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Generate the short forms by code from the full replies or keep only the short form, and reference them by id from the system prompt.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. The assistant searches a private product catalog (rag.search) and a live web search API (web.search) through one MCP server, then answers with a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds and an on-screen comparison table with citations. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
